title: Decode a delay slot that lies past the function's end (PR #304, issue #370)
problem: A branch in a function's last word got a synthetic NOP delay slot; the real instruction was dropped silently (FIFA Street 2 crash per #370).
approach: decodeFunction decodes one extra word after end when the last instruction has a delay slot. Extended here: slices keep the trailing delay slot and the emitter decodes it from the ELF section with a warning.
scope_evidence: MIPS executes the word at branch+4 for every branch (except an untaken likely branch).
reference: MIPS R5900 branch delay slot semantics

evidence.analysis: diff read; both slicing sites in ps2_recompiler.cpp found to cut the same way
tests_added: a delay slot past the function's end is still translated
a delay slot past the decoded range is translated from the ELF section
a delay slot outside every section still falls back to a NOP
evidence.regression: ps2x_tests 454/454; mutation (emitter fallback disabled) fails the section test

limitations: Configured instruction patches are not applied to a delay slot recovered by the emitter fallback.

title: VCALLMSR starts from CMSAR0 instead of vi[27] (PR #268, issue #262)
problem: Generated code read ctx->vi[27] from uint16_t vi[16]: out-of-bounds UB, wrong microprogram (CoD: WaW Final Fronts AI/camera failures per #262).
scope_evidence: VCALLMSR always uses CMSAR0 (PCSX2 COP2.cpp: vu0ExecMicro(VU0.VI[REG_CMSAR0])).

tests_added: VCALLMSR starts the microprogram from CMSAR0, not a VI array slot

limitations: vi[] is still 16 entries; the other VU0 control registers keep their separate fields.

title: VU0 macro LQI/LQD/SQI/SQD/ILWR/ISWR operands and VU0 data memory (PR #310, issue #309)
problem: SQI/SQD swapped fs/it (OOB vi[16..31] write); all six instructions accessed EE RAM 0x0000-0x3FF0 instead of VU0 data memory (ICO camera corruption per #309).
approach: Correct field decode; access runtime->memory().getVU0Data() with qword wrap. Extended here: vi0/vf0 stay hardwired.
scope_evidence: Encoding and semantics match PCSX2 VUops.cpp _vuSQI/_vuLQD/_vuILWR/_vuISWR.

tests_added: VU0 LQI/LQD/SQI/SQD decode fields and use VU0 data memory
VU0 ILWR/ISWR address VU0 data memory by qword and field
VU0 macro loads/stores keep vi0 and vf0 hardwired

limitations: VU0 addresses 0x4000+ (VU1 register mirror) wrap inside 4 KiB instead of mapping VU1 registers.

title: EE invocation stacks off the main thread's stack, reused per thread (issue #258)
problem: Interrupt/callback stacks were carved from the top of RAM where SetupThread puts the main stack (Ridge Racer V game loop died per #258), and were never reclaimed (PR #298 fallback shown to re-alias in #347).
approach: Own design: low region [0x90000, min(0xF0000, ELF start)) first (PR #298's tested range), free list on thread dormancy, cleared on reset, logged fallback.
scope_evidence: Any title that takes an interrupt during a nested call on the main thread.

tests_added: async callback stacks come from below the ELF before the top of RAM
threads that come and go reuse invocation stacks instead of exhausting them
evidence.regression: ps2x_tests 454/454, ps2xIOP ctest 4/4; mutation (no release) fails the churn test

limitations: A title that loads an ELF below 0x90000 gets no low region and uses the logged fallback.

title: SetupThread(-1) records the stack base like CreateThread (issue #259)
problem: GuestThread::stack was a top for the SetupThread main thread and a base for CreateThread threads.
approach: Store top - size; returned $sp and stack location unchanged.
scope_evidence: Kernel bookkeeping used by ReferThreadStatus for every title.

tests_added: SetupThread exposes stable main stack metadata through ReferThreadStatus (updated expectation)

limitations: For SetupThread(-1) the runtime still tops the stack at 0x02000000 - size; Play! uses RAM size - 4 KiB. Not changed without more evidence.

title: D_ENABLEW is visible at D_ENABLER; both reset to 0x1201 (PR #284, issue #257)
problem: The DMAC enable register's write and read ports were unrelated slots, so suspend/resume polls spun forever (Ridge Racer V froze per #257).
approach: A write to D_ENABLEW lands in both slots; both start at 0x1201 (CPND clear).
scope_evidence: Every title that suspends the DMAC through D_ENABLEW and polls D_ENABLER.
reference: PCSX2 pcsx2/Dmac.cpp dmacWrite32 DMAC_ENABLEW, pcsx2/Hw.cpp hwReset; ps2tek DMAC registers
upstream_equivalent: ran-j/PS2Recomp#284 (open); PR #372 contains an overlapping mirror hunk without the reset value

tests_added: DMAC D_ENABLER reads 0x1201 after reset with CPND clear
DMAC D_ENABLEW writes are visible at D_ENABLER
DMAC suspend and resume polls through D_ENABLEW and D_ENABLER terminate

limitations: Channel kicks still run immediately while CPND is set (no queued-DMA model).

title: VIF stall after the I bit (VSS/VFS/VIS) with FBRST.STC/STP/FBK/RST (PR #295, adapted)
problem: The I bit raised INTC but the VIF kept processing; games expecting to run their VIF handler before the rest of the stream saw the data processed too early.
approach: PR #295's held-data/held-DMA design, adjusted to PCSX2: MARK with the I bit does not stall, ERR.MII masks everything, a DMA ending on the I-bit code completes, VIF0 included, VIF register reads mapped to the VIF state.
scope_evidence: Hardware VIF behaviour for every title using the I bit.

tests_added: VIF1 I bit stalls the VIF after its command until FBRST.STC
VIF1 MARK with the I bit interrupts without stalling
VIF1 ERR.MII masks the I bit
VIF1 DMA behind an I-bit stall completes only after FBRST.STC
VIF1 DMA whose last code carries the I bit completes while VIS stays set
VIF1 FBRST.RST drops held data and releases a held DMA
VIF1 FBRST.STP stalls incoming data until STC
VIF0 I bit stalls until VIF0_FBRST.STC
an INTC_VIF1 handler releases the VIF1 stall with FBRST.STC
evidence.regression: ps2x_tests 480/480, ps2xIOP 4/4; each stall rule's test fails with the rule reverted

limitations: Stalls caused by VU1/PATH waits (FLUSH, MSCAL busy) are still not modelled; FBK does not cancel an in-flight DMA.
